text: Large Language Models, or LLMs, are computer programs trained on massive amounts of text from books, websites, and articles. By finding patterns in this data, they learn to predict the next word in a sentence, which allows them to generate surprisingly human-like responses. When you use an LLM, you give it a prompt—a question or instruction. This is where prompt engineering matters: clear, specific prompts usually produce better answers. These models can write essays, translate languages, and even help with coding. However, they have limits. They don’t truly understand meaning; they often make up facts, and their knowledge stops at a certain date. So, while powerful, they work best with careful human guidance.
